channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Genesis AI Hits $3.5B Valuation in Robotics Bet
item.description: Genesis AI has raised $500 million at a $3.5 billion valuation as it develops general-purpose robots designed to eventually perform complex tasks with human-level dexterity. CEO and co-founder Zhou Xian discusses plans to scale its robotic AI model, manufacture its first fully US-made robots next year and ramp up production. He also explains why Genesis is taking a full-stack approach spanning AI, hardware and individual robot components. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic IPO Highlights AI’s Private Market Wealth
item.description: Anthropic’s IPO is highlighting just how much value can be created before public investors ever get a chance to buy in. Athena Capital founder and managing partner Isabelle Freidheim discusses what Anthropic’s potential $1.4 trillion valuation says about the growth of private markets, and how its debut could create a path for other late-stage technology companies to go public. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Faces First Earnings Test Since Huang’s Exit
item.description: Nvidia reports earnings for the first time since Jensen Huang’s surprise departure, putting the chipmaker’s 70% growth outlook and the broader AI trade back in focus. JPMorgan Asset Management’s Stephanie Aliaga discusses why strong compute demand remains intact despite leadership uncertainty, what investors need to hear from Nvidia on growth and China, and how Anthropic’s IPO could give public-market investors a new window into the economics of frontier AI. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Jensen Huang Signals He’s Ready for Nvidia Comeback
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down Jensen Huang's statement saying he would be willing to return as CEO if the board agreed, and that he has received an "outpouring" of support from people calling for his return. Plus, President Trump held talks on AI collaboration with partner countries India, Australia, and Japan, amid rising competition with China and ahead of his meeting with China's Xi Jinping; and California Attorney General Rob Bonta joins to discuss why he is taking OpenAI to court over rogue AI agents. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: States Press for Scrutiny in Sale of Chatbot Said to Harm Kids
item.description: Dozens of state attorneys asked a federal judge to impose extra scrutiny on the proposed sale of an artificial intelligence chatbot that allegedly encouraged suicidal thoughts in a 14-year-old boy who killed himself.
item.dc:creator: Steven Church

item.title: Nvidia Scandal Has Raised ‘Red Flags,’ California AG Says
item.description: California Attorney General Rob Bonta said that his office is looking into aspects of the scandal that’s engulfed Nvidia Corp. and its former chief executive officer, Jensen Huang.
item.dc:creator: Erik Larson and Ed Ludlow

item.title: Nvidia to Face Its New AI Reality
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Nvidia takes center stage, reporting without Jensen Huang as the tech trade faces fresh pressure. Home Depot kicks off retail earnings as consumers keep spending, while Disney beats expectations and Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO demand pushes pricing to the top of the range or higher. Plus, Meredith Whitney joins us on consumer strain, AI risks and whether the fallout could spread to banks and the broader economy. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: OpenAI Unveils New Astra AI Model After Scrapping Prior Release
item.description: OpenAI is releasing a new version of its most advanced Astra artificial intelligence model nearly two months after the company scrapped a prior update to establish stronger safeguards for the technology.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Metz

item.title: US Electronic Spy Agency Suffers Classified Network Outage
item.description: The National Security Agency is suffering an outage of a classified computer network it uses for internal communications and other daily work functions, according to a US official and another person familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Jake Bleiberg and Natalia Drozdiak

item.title: JPMorgan Warns Leveraged-Loan Defaults Set to Double in 2027
item.description: Defaults in the leveraged-loan market are expected to more than double to 4.5% next year, reaching levels not seen since 2024 as heavily indebted companies face mounting financial pressure, according to analysts at JPMorgan Chase & Co.
item.dc:creator: Aaron Weinman

item.title: New Street's Ferragu Sees Strong Case to Buy Nvidia Shares Ahead of Earnings
item.description: Pierre Ferragu of New Street Research maintains a buy rating on Nvidia shares and says the recent selloff strengthens the case to buy. He says the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang won't affect near-term earnings. Ferragu speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Read Jensen Huang’s Statement Offering a Return as Nvidia CEO
item.description: After his chaotic exit from Nvidia Corp. last week, former Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang said he’s received an “outpouring” of support from people calling for his return.
item.dc:creator: Ian King

item.title: Big US Grid Proposes Overhaul to Speed Data Center Hook Ups
item.description: The largest US grid is proposing a “fast energization” plan to speed up connection for data centers and power plants in response to criticism from regulators that PJM Interconnection LLC is struggling to keep pace with surging demand while costs rise for consumers.
item.dc:creator: Naureen S. Malik

item.title: Take-Two’s Firaxis, Maker of ‘Civilization,’ Cuts a Third of Its Staff
item.description: The Maryland-based development studio behind the Civilization and XCOM franchises, laid off around 60 people on Tuesday
item.dc:creator: Jason Schreier

item.title: Compute Futures Aim to Hedge AI Risks
item.description: Carmen Li, founder and CEO of Silicon Data and CEO of the Compute Exchange joined Bloomberg Open Interest to talk about how compute futures could give financiers and AI companies a way to hedge shifting GPU costs and supply risks. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: De Nvidia a los humanoides: EE.UU. vs. China: en la carrera por la IA
item.description: Tanto EE.UU. como China ven en la inteligencia artificial el nuevo epicentro de su rivalidad económica. El presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump, ha declarado que “quien gane en IA, gana”. La cuestión es si ambas potencias pueden dejar de lado sus diferencias y cooperar para crear un entorno seguro y sostenible para el desarrollo de esta tecnología.
item.dc:creator: Saritha Rai, Colum Murphy and Josh Xiao

item.title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang Open to Rejoining as CEO Pending Board Decision
item.description: Former Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang expressed willingness to return to the helm after his dramatic ouster last week, though the board isn’t currently considering such an idea.
item.dc:creator: Ian King

item.title: Trump Seeks $50 Billion for Airspace Upgrades After Outage
item.description: President Donald Trump’s administration formally requested $50.1 billion to overhaul the US airspace system, citing an “urgent need” to modernize the critical infrastructure after a technology breakdown grounded flights nationwide last week.
item.dc:creator: Allyson Versprille and Erik Wasson

item.title: EM Stocks Retreat Ahead of Nvidia, While Currencies Gain Ground
item.description: Emerging-market stocks retreated for the fourth straight session as upcoming earnings from Nvidia Corp. kept traders on edge, while currencies extended gains after reports of another US outage pushed the dollar lower.
item.dc:creator: Ray Ndlovu and Nicolle Yapur

item.title: Anthropic Faces a Longer Wait Than SpaceX to Join Indexes
item.description: Anthropic’s planned initial public offering could generate billions of dollars in demand from index-tracking funds, though the artificial intelligence startup may have to wait longer than SpaceX did to join two major stock benchmarks.
item.dc:creator: Lu Wang
